reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: AI algorithms harming children's mental health
themes.definition: AI-driven algorithms, social media and chatbots framed as harming children's and teenagers' mental health, with calls for health-and-safety style regulation and age limits.
themes.inclusion: Include passages on AI-optimized social media, chatbots or algorithms harming minors, and on age verification, phone bans or platform duty of care for children.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general youth education or AI skills passages that do not concern harm to children.
themes.boundary_cases: Passages about social media harms without explicit AI mention count when they continue an argument where AI-driven algorithms were named.

examples.quote: Social media algorithms are constantly improved by AI to keep children online for the maximum amount of time
We don't want our kids to share their intimate thoughts and feelings with an AI chatbot.
Digital technology is no different than any other industry that needs to operate under health and safety regulations.
The brains of our children are being rewired, and their development changed on an almost unimaginable scale.

themes.label: Unaccountable power of big tech companies
themes.definition: Concern that a few large technology companies wield more power than states and are not accountable.
themes.inclusion: Include passages about tech companies' outsized economic power, lack of accountability, or AI concentrating power in few corporations.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages about state-level digital divides without corporate power framing.
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for tech companies to join governance processes fit here and in AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: a few very large technology companies, with more economic muscle than most of the countries represented here
concentrate immense power in the hands of a few multinational corporations

themes.label: Global framework like a COP for AI
themes.definition: Calls to put AI regulation on a global footing, e.g. a conference of the parties for AI modeled on climate governance.
themes.inclusion: Include passages proposing global regimes, COP-style frameworks or agile global governance for AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude national regulatory measures only (e.g. school phone bans).
themes.boundary_cases: Praise of UN advisory body reports fits here and in AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: Eventually, what we may need is a conference of the parties for AI, with the participation not just of countries but also of the global technology companies.
with AI there is no such framework

themes.label: Support for UN AI bodies and reports
themes.definition: Endorsement of UN AI institutions: SG High-Level Advisory Body report, Scientific Panel, Global Dialogue, Global Digital Compact.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit praise or welcome of named UN AI bodies, reports or compacts.
themes.boundary_cases: If the UN mention is only a conditional ('if the GDC is to have effect') it still counts.

examples.quote: I welcome the United Nations establishment of the independent international scientific panel on AI and the global dialogue on artificial intelligence governance.
presented just a few days ago by the High-Level Advisory Body on Artificial Intelligence, established by the Secretary- General

themes.label: Transformative promise versus extraordinary harm
themes.definition: AI presented as a game-changing general-purpose technology with great benefits but also capacity for extraordinary harm (deepfakes, control, job displacement).
themes.inclusion: Include passages explicitly weighing AI's transformative benefits against its dangers.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages that only describe harms to children.
themes.boundary_cases: Deepfake/disinformation mentions within the duality framing can also be coded AI_DISINFORMATION.

examples.quote: However, AI also has the potential to do extraordinary harm.
generative AI is used to create more and more convincing deepfakes, designed to spread misinformation and disinformation

themes.label: Greek AI pilots in public services
themes.definition: Description of the country's own AI strategy and pilots in education, health, and disaster prevention.
themes.inclusion: Include passages describing national AI programmes or deployments.
themes.exclusion: Exclude hypothetical benefits not tied to national action.
themes.boundary_cases: National child-safety tools (Kids Wallet) belong to AI_CHILD_PROTECTION rather than here.

examples.quote: Greece is pursuing a visionary yet practical AI strategy through pilot programs in areas such as education, healthcare, and natural disaster prevention.

value.rationale: All Greek passages; the dominant thread is AI-driven platforms harming children's mental health and the need for safety regulation. They also discuss big-tech power, global/UN governance, the promise-peril of AI, and Greece's national AI pilots.
